content:
A partner who likes the plant has not agreed to give. You still have to ask. In this meeting you name one amount, or one recurring amount with an end date, and you leave room for a no.

Follow-up is the date the two of you set. You own it. You write what they said. You do not record a gift or write the receipt. Raising Outside Support already assigns the ask to you and the gift records to the Financial Leader. This article does not move that line.

---

## Ask for one stated amount

Bring one number from the first-year budget. Tie it to a line, or to a stated share of the remaining gap, and put an end date on it. "Help if you can" is not a request. A menu of amounts is not a request either.

A monthly commitment needs the amount, the first month, and the last month. "For as long as you can" cannot go in the budget.

Use the figures you built with your coach. [First Year Budget Planning](/wiki/administrative/financial/first-year-budget-planning) is where you document outside commitments and their conditions or time limits.

Ask them to give to the church for that line. Do not ask them to pay you, and do not promise a tax deduction.

---

## Hold the meeting

This meeting includes the amount. Explain the need, name the figure, and ask. Do not save the amount for a later visit.

- [ ] Write the budget line, the amount, and the dates.
- [ ] Get the church legal name and the giving instructions from the Financial Leader.
- [ ] Write what the gift will pay for, and what it will not pay for.
- [ ] Choose the response date you will offer if they do not answer today.
- [ ] Decide what you will say if they refuse, and stop there.

Say how you know them. Name the need and the amount. Say the gift goes to the church. Ask whether they will take part. Then stop talking.

Do not inflate the Core Group, the launch date, or what their gift will accomplish. Date any past event you mention.

If they say yes, repeat the amount, the dates, and any restriction. Ask when they expect to send the first gift. That date is their plan, not proof the gift left their account. If they offer less, write their number. Do not bargain them up. If they say no, thank them and close the ask. Do not offer a smaller number in the same breath.

Accept a restriction only for a fund the elders have already set up. Read [Designated Giving Policies](/wiki/administrative/financial/designated-giving-policies) before you agree, and have the Financial Leader confirm the wording. Refuse "for the planter to use as needed."

A partner church gets the same request. Ask the pastors or elders. A letter uses the same line, amount, dates, and church legal name you would say aloud.

If they ask what another household gives, do not answer. You may share the budget gap and the nameless Core Group total you already receive. Tax questions go to their adviser.

If they try to hand you cash or a check, do not open it or write the amount. Get it to the Financial Leader the same day, with a second person present.

<Callout type="warning">
Read the amount, then wait. Do not fill the silence, shrink the number, or tell them what a gift would prove about their faith. A refusal is a complete answer.
</Callout>

---

## Name the date and the owner

If they do not answer in the meeting, agree on a response date before you leave. Ask whether you may reconnect on that date about this request. If they say no, there is no money follow-up.

There is no church-wide count of days for a partner answer. A partner who asked you to call Thursday is waiting on Thursday. A partner with no date is not late. Set the date, or close the ask. Do not copy a Vision Meeting follow-up timetable onto this conversation.

Your name goes on the row. You lead the request, so you own the reconnect. Do not hand the amount conversation to a Core Group member. A stale row means you have not made that reconnect. It does not mean you are behind on follow-ups someone else owns.

Leave any non-money check-in with its current owner. The money question stays on your row.

You may ask whether they want occasional news of the plant, with no amounts in it. That permission is separate. News is not another chance to ask.

<Callout type="insight">
A finished follow-up is an answer, not a deposit. Close the row when they answer, not when you wish they had.
</Callout>

---

## Follow up once

On the agreed date, contact them the way they allowed. Remind them of the amount. Ask for their answer. Then stop.

- [ ] Yes. Repeat the amount, one gift or recurring, the start, the end, and any restriction. The Financial Leader sends the giving instructions.
- [ ] No. Thank them. Write no. Do not ask again.
- [ ] Still undecided. Thank them and close the ask. Do not open another waiting period.

One follow-up is the limit when they asked for time. Another check-in is pressure, and it leaves a number nobody agreed to.

Thank them in private for the conversation. Do not thank them later for a figure from the books. [Principles of Financial Accountability](/wiki/administrative/financial/principles-of-financial-accountability) already keeps individual amounts away from the Senior Pastor. The amount you asked for is the request, not a giving report.

---

## Report what they said, not what arrived

Keep an ask log. Send the Financial Leader a copy of each closed row. Do not add payment results to yours.

| What you write | What you leave off |
| --- | --- |
| Who you asked, and the amount you asked for | Whether a gift arrived |
| Yes, no, or closed without a decision | A deposit date or receipt number |
| The amount and dates they agreed to, if they agreed | Any household giving history |
| The response date, and that you own the follow-up | A note that you checked the bank |
| A restriction they named, unconfirmed until the Financial Leader accepts it | Their tax position |

Put a yes in the budget as an outside commitment, with the conditions and end date. Change the budget if they change the commitment. Do not spend the money because they said yes.

"We are for you" is not a yes. "Send me something" is not a yes.

<Callout type="important">
IRS Publication 526 for 2025, checked October 26, 2026, says a contribution is usually made at unconditional delivery. A promissory note given to a charity is not a contribution until the payments are made. Publication 1771, checked the same day, describes an acknowledgment of a contribution received, including the amount of any monetary contribution. Confirm the current publications before you describe a gift, and send donors to their own tax adviser.
</Callout>

The Financial Leader writes that acknowledgment after a gift is received. Follow [Donor Receipts and Giving Statements](/wiki/administrative/financial/donor-receipts-and-giving-statements). Publication 1771 says the date of the contribution is the date the donor gave it. A spoken yes does not belong on that page. You do not draft it, sign it, or read the copy that shows what they paid.

If the meeting included a meal or anything else of value, tell the Financial Leader before an acknowledgment goes out.

If a partner says the gift is on the way, thank them for partnering with the church. Do not match their words to the books. If they ask whether it arrived, send them to the Financial Leader.

If you asked only one partner for a line, a received total can name them. Do not ask the amount, and do not use that guess when you preach, pray in public, or decide how to treat them.

---

## Keep news separate from receipts

You can tell a partner how the plant is going. Date the story. Leave every amount out, and do not say whether their gift arrived.

Public thanks stay general. Thank partners as a group. Do not name a household and a figure in a sermon, a prayer, or a Core Group meeting.

Partner commitments are not Core Group generosity. Report them on their own line. A funded line does not prove the core is giving.

Everyfield does not store this meeting, the ask log, or the gift. A note that funding looks sufficient is not cash received. The app does not judge the ask. Keep the log and the books in the church's own records.

---

## Mistakes that distort the answer

**Leaving without a number.** No amount and no response date means you did not hold this meeting.

**Hearing a yes they did not say.** Prayer and excitement are not commitments. Write the words they used.

**Following up with no owner.** Your name goes on this row.

**Writing the receipt yourself.** The Financial Leader writes it, and only after the church has received the gift.

**Checking whether they paid.** Looking up the gift is how amount knowledge starts. Do not start.

---

<Callout type="scripture">
*"Each one must do just as he has purposed in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver."* — 2 Corinthians 9:7 (LSB)
</Callout>

Ask for the amount. Accept their answer. Leave the gift with the Financial Leader.
excerpt: You ask a financial partner for one stated amount, set a response date, and record the answer. A yes is a commitment, not money received.
title: Asking Financial Partners and Following Up

sources.claim: The date of a contribution is the date the donor gave it to the organization, so an acknowledgment describes a gift received rather than a promise.
sources.quote: The date of the contribution is the date the donor gave the charitable organization the contribution.

sources.claim: A donor generally needs a contemporaneous written acknowledgment before claiming a federal income tax deduction for any single contribution of $250 or more.
sources.quote: A donor cannot claim a federal income tax deduction for any single contribution valued at $250 or more unless the donor obtains a contemporaneous written acknowledgment of the contribution from the donee charitable organization.

sources.claim: A written acknowledgment of a monetary contribution states the amount contributed.
sources.quote: the amount of any monetary contribution

sources.claim: When no goods or services were provided, the acknowledgment says so.
sources.quote: a statement that no goods or services were provided by the organization in return for the contribution, if that was the case

sources.claim: An IRS sample acknowledgment thanks the donor for a contribution the organization received on a stated date and says whether goods or services were provided.
sources.quote: Thank you for your cash contribution of $300 that (organization’s name) received on December 12, 2015. No goods or services were provided in exchange for your contribution.

sources.claim: A contribution is usually made when it is unconditionally delivered, so a spoken yes is not yet a gift.
sources.quote: Usually, you make a contribution at the time of its unconditional delivery.

sources.claim: A promissory note delivered to a charity is not a contribution until the donor makes the note payments.
sources.quote: If you issue and deliver a promissory note to a charity as a contribution, it isn’t a contribution until you make the note payments.

claim_check.notes: Owner review by Sebastian; no model review per his 2026-10-26 instruction.

rulings: Bryan ruled B2 = Option A: "A specific request" (2026-10-26 1:31 PM ET).

Wording call: title is Asking Financial Partners and Following Up rather than the backlog title Meeting and Following Up with Financial Partners, so the title names the ruled request. Slug kept as the brief's suggested path. Phase 0, with the other financial articles, because the meeting belongs with first-year budget work before launch. sort_order 11, the next unused integer in this section after the unpublished B1 draft took 10. Seed itself still has 10 free.

Wording call on who asks: Bryan's B1 Option B ruling assigns the ask to the planter. This draft teaches you, the planter, as the authorized fundraiser. It does not add a second person who may discuss amounts.

Wording call on the shape of the request: one stated amount, or one recurring amount with a start and an end. Not a menu of amounts, and not a smaller counter-offer if they refuse. If they offer less, record their number and do not bargain up.

Wording call on timing: no universal donor timetable. The response date is the one you and the partner set. C22's warm and cold contact timing is not applied here as a day count. One follow-up if they asked for time, matching Raising Outside Support. If they are still undecided, close the ask.

Wording call on ownership: the planter owns this follow-up because the planter owns the ask. Do not assign the amount conversation to a Core Group member. C01 and C13 still apply. The owner is written on the row so a stale partner follow-up is not treated as proof the planter is behind on follow-ups they do not own.

Wording call on Publication 1771: its pledge-card language is for payroll-deduction records, not a partner's spoken commitment. This draft does not use that payroll rule as the meeting rule. A promise stays off the acknowledgment because Publication 1771 describes a contribution received, and Publication 526 times a contribution at unconditional delivery. A promissory note is cited only as the closest IRS statement that a written promise is not yet a gift. A spoken yes is recorded as a commitment, not described as a promissory note.

Wording call on news: permission to hear plant news, with no amounts, is separate from permission to reconnect about the request. A no to the money follow-up can still allow news. No contact at all means stop.

Applied Bryan's C06 ruling: partner commitments are outside support, not Core Group generosity. Applied the published boundary that the Senior Pastor does not receive individual gift amounts. A single-partner budget line can still reveal a household, so you do not use that inference.
